result:
Solution B is more likely correct, though I can't fully verify the classification from memory.

**Solution A** rests on a classification that appears to be invented. It claims the three subgroups are the full group and the subgroups of index 2 and index p. Its justification ("p-part has index 1 or p, p'-part has index 1 or 2, not both non-full") is asserted without derivation. The arithmetic is internally consistent: the sum is p^{n-2}(p-1)(3p+2)/2. But that rests on the unsupported subgroup list.

**Solution B** gives the subgroups of orders p-1, p^{n-1}, and p^{n-1}(p-1). These correspond to the p'-part of Aut(G) (the subgroup of order p-1), the Sylow p-subgroup, and the full group. This structure matches what I recall of the published classification of almost commutative Terwilliger algebras of orbit Schur rings over cyclic p-groups, though I can't confirm the exact statement. The orders are distinct for odd p and n ≥ 2, since p-1 ≠ p^{n-1}. The sum is:

(p-1) + p^{n-1} + p^{n-1}(p-1) = p^n + p - 1

This is correct.

WINNER: B
